what: Recorded enclosures from the worked example: L = (1+x)*Dx^2 + Dx annihilates ln(1+x); certified transport of (f, f') = (0, 1) along [0, 1/2] at eps 1e-40, algorithm='naive'. The transported value is ln(3/2). Both records come from the reference build (SageMath 10.7 + ore_algebra 0.5); the battery's engine-free leg recomputes ln(3/2) independently in pure Python integer arithmetic and verifies these recorded balls contain it and are internally consistent.

records.source: raw transition-matrix entry (0,1), printed ball at 42 decimal digits
certified_transport() house-layer call (entry re-wrapped in RealBallField(430)), printed ball at 41 decimal digits

notes: printed_radius is the radius of the DECIMAL-PRINTED ball (it absorbs the print-rounding of the midpoint), so containment of the true value is checked against printed_radius; certified_radius is the internal Arb radius of the same ball. abs_err_vs_ln32_upper is the recorded upper bound on |ball - ln(3/2)| against a 300-bit evaluation of the logarithm; containment implies it is at most 2*certified_radius plus the comparison ball's own (negligible) radius.
